title: 第120章乱世知人心第119章剑指不平事
content_zh:
盛唐永安二十七年，秋，霜风骤起，席卷京华。
皇城的琉璃瓦被连夜的冷霜覆上一层惨白，晨光斜落，映不出百年王朝的恢弘盛景，反倒衬得整座紫禁城萧索空寂，处处透着朽木将倾的颓败。御史台的值房清冷寂静，窗棂外是簌簌飘落的枯叶，窗内是萧琰执笔凝思的孤影。他指尖压着厚厚一叠卷宗，纸页层层叠叠，写满了江南洪涝灾情、西北边军溃弊、地方官吏贪腐的罪证，笔墨沉凝，字字沉重，压得人胸口发闷。
萧琰今年三十有二，入仕十二载，从一介寒门新科进士，熬到如今的御史中丞。身居言官要职，掌监察百官、弹劾奸佞之权，在外人看来，他年少得志、身居要位，是朝堂之中前途无量的新锐重臣。可唯有萧琰自己清楚，这十二年宦海沉浮，他见过的从不是盛世清明、朝堂公理，而是层层叠叠的腐朽、藏于衣冠之下的贪婪，是乱世将临前，彻底崩坏的人心世道。
世人惯于称颂大晟百年基业，说四海承平、国泰民安。可身在局中，萧琰早已看透，这所谓的盛世，不过是权贵勋贵粉饰出来的虚假皮囊。内里早已蛀空溃烂，皇权孱弱、外戚专权、宦官窃政、党争不休、苛税连年、民不聊生。乱世从不是一夜崩塌的倾覆，而是日复一日的溃烂，是人心先烂，社稷再倾。十二年浮沉，他遍历朝堂百态，看透君臣伪善、同僚凉薄、权贵贪婪，终是彻悟一句话：乱世最真见人心，浊朝最明辨善恶。
他的半生清醒，皆来自半生血泪。萧琰本是青州望族，萧氏世代书香，累世忠良。其父萧景渊，曾是当朝御史大夫，一生刚正不阿，以肃贪治乱、匡扶社稷为己任，从不趋炎附势，从不畏惧权贵。彼时朝堂太尉司马睿权倾朝野，结党营私，把持朝政，暗中克扣三边塞外军饷，中饱私囊，致使边军粮草断绝、甲胄残破，无数戍边将士冻饿而死，边境防线日渐松弛。满朝文武畏惧司马睿权势，无人敢言一字，唯有萧景渊连夜上奏，罗列其二十三条大罪，字字铿锵，句句诛心，誓要为国除奸、整肃朝纲。
那一夜的血色火光，是萧琰一生无法磨灭的印记。刑场之上，父亲临刑无惧，只留下一句遗言：朝堂浊乱，人心贪妄，乱世将至，守心最难。彼时的萧琰尚且年少，满心悲愤，只恨奸佞当道、世道不公，却尚未真正懂得，父亲口中的人心贪妄、乱世之祸，从不止于一两个权奸，而是整个朝堂的集体溃烂，是无数衣冠之人的集体失心。
蛰伏三年，萧琰隐姓埋名，寒窗苦读，磨去少年戾气，沉淀心性风骨。他没有选择隐世避俗、苟且偷生，而是执意重入京城、再踏朝堂。旁人问他为何自投罗网、重入浊世，他只答：若忠臣皆避世，良臣皆缄口，这大晟江山，便真的彻底无药可救了。他要入仕，要立朝，要亲眼看着浊朝乱象，要以一己微薄之力，守一缕朝堂清明，告慰满门忠魂。
弱冠之末，萧琰重登金榜，以殿试二甲第一的名次入朝为官。他摒弃所有家世旧怨，不攀附权贵，不投靠派系，孤身一人，立于波诡云谲的朝堂之中。初入仕途时，他仍存少年赤诚，坚信公道自在人心，坚信忠善必有回响，坚信只要为官清正、履职尽责，便能拨乱反正、安民济世。可十二年光阴，无数次亲眼所见、亲身所历、心寒彻骨的经历，一点点碾碎了他所有的天真期许，让他彻底洞悉了乱世朝堂的本质。
如今的大晟，早已是外盛内枯、金玉其外败絮其中。永安帝在位二十七年，早年尚有励精图治之志，可晚年倦怠朝政，沉迷长生丹药，沉溺深宫享乐，终日不问国事、不理万民。皇权日渐旁落，形同虚设，偌大朝堂，彻底沦为外戚、宦官、世家三股势力博弈的棋局。三方势力相互制衡、彼此倾轧、此消彼长，无人心系社稷安危，无人体恤黎民疾苦，所有人的毕生所求，唯有权位、名利、财富。
外戚以太尉司马睿为首，依托后宫贵妃之势，把持朝堂军政要务，掌控京畿兵权，子弟亲族遍布朝野，占据三公九卿半数职位，肆意敛财、安插私党、打压异己，气焰滔天，无人敢制衡。宦官以司礼监掌印太监魏秉谦为首，手握批红之权，代帝理政，掌控朝堂文书、诏令出入，暗中结交寒门官员、地方藩吏，结党营私，蒙蔽圣听，肆意篡改政令、曲解圣意，从中渔利。老牌世家则盘踞朝野百年，固守门第之见，相互联姻抱团，垄断朝堂清流之名，看似清高自持，实则明哲保身、坐观成败，谁得势便依附谁，无半分家国风骨。
除了三大核心派系，余下百官更是人心涣散、各怀鬼胎。有人趋炎附势、左右逢源，只求安稳度日、步步高升；有人贪婪成性、搜刮民脂，将官职视作牟利商贾；有人庸碌无为、尸位素餐，身居高位却一事无成；有人胆小怯懦、缄口不言，眼见奸佞横行、民生疾苦，却始终明哲保身、不敢多言。偌大一个大晟朝堂，数百名文武官员，真正心怀家国、心系万民、坚守本心者，寥寥无几。
萧琰立于这浑浊棋局之中，如同孤舟浮于沧海，四面皆浊，唯己独清。十二年里，他见过太多虚伪嘴脸，看透太多凉薄人心，渐渐懂得，乱世之乱，首乱在心。山河崩坏始于人心崩坏，社稷倾覆始于人心沦丧。太平盛世，尚有礼法约束、道德束缚，人心尚且知廉耻、懂忠义、守底线，可乱世将至，法度松弛、皇权孱弱、无人制衡，人性深处的贪婪、自私、阴狠、狡诈尽数暴露，所有的忠义礼法、家国大义，都成了可以随意抛弃、肆意践踏的空谈。
今日卯时，天尚未亮，晨雾浓重，笼罩整座皇城。午门之外，车马骈阗、冠盖如云，本该肃穆庄重的入朝时刻，却处处充斥着市井般的钻营与谄媚。官员们三五成群，低声攀谈，无人探讨边防军务、民生利弊，句句皆是派系动向、圣上心迹、升迁机遇。有人低声打探贵妃近日喜好，想要投其所好、攀附外戚；有人暗中打听司礼监动向，想要依附宦官、谋求便利；有人相互吹捧寒暄，假意交好，实则各怀算计、彼此提防。
萧琰一身素色青袍，立于人群最末，身姿挺拔，眉眼清冷却无半分戾气。他早已习惯这般喧嚣虚伪的场景，也早已看透这群衣冠楚楚之人的真实面目。人前皆是谦谦君子、忠良贤臣，人后皆是蝇营狗苟、自私自利。十二年官场历练，磨平了他的年少锐气，却未曾磨掉他的本心风骨，只让他学会了冷眼旁观、静默洞悉，不掺和派系纷争，不参与名利博弈，只守御史本职，察百官之过，悯万民之苦。
今日朝会，是月中最隆重的大朝会，本该决议数件关乎社稷存亡的大事。其一，江南七郡秋雨连绵三月不绝，江河泛滥、堤坝崩塌，万顷良田被淹，数十万户百姓流离失所，饥寒交迫，灾情惨烈，亟待朝廷赈灾安民、修缮堤坝、减免赋税。其二，西北蛮族趁秋高马肥，屡次大举犯边，攻破三座边关要塞，劫掠边境村镇，屠戮边地百姓，而大晟边军军备废弛、粮草短缺、军心涣散，守将畏敌避战、节节败退，西北边防岌岌可危。其三，天下州县苛税繁重，地方官吏层层加派赋税、肆意摊派徭役，百姓不堪重负，多地已有流民聚众滋事，隐隐有动乱之兆。
桩桩件件，皆是亡国乱政之隐患，皆是关乎万千百姓生死、大晟江山存续的要务。可萧琰心中清楚，这般危局，在朝堂权贵眼中，不过是可供博弈的棋子、借机牟利的契机，从无人真正放在心上。
金銮殿上，香烟袅袅，庄严肃穆，高位之上，永安帝垂眸静坐，面色倦怠，双目浑浊，早已无半分帝王锐气。他端坐龙椅，看似掌控天下，实则早已被深宫享乐消磨心智，对朝堂乱象、天下疾苦，尽数视而不见、听而不闻。他所求的，唯有皇权稳固、长生久视、余生安乐，至于百姓流离、边关危亡、社稷隐患，皆不值一提。
朝会伊始，户部尚书率先出列启奏。此人隶属外戚派系，是司马睿一手提拔的心腹，身居户部要职，掌天下钱粮赋税，却从不思安民理财，唯以中饱私囊、补贴外戚宗族为己任。他手持奏折，言辞恳切，句句哭诉西北边军之难，谎称边关粮草断绝、军械老旧、兵力不足，恳请陛下拨付五百万两白银、十万石粮草，用以重整边军、抵御外敌。
此言一出，萧琰心底一片寒凉。他三日前刚收到边关密报，朝廷上半年拨付的三百万两军饷、二十万石粮草，大半被边军守将与户部官员私分克扣，层层流转，最终落入司马睿外戚集团的私库，真正抵达军营、用于军士的不足三成。如今边军溃败，非是朝廷拨付不足，而是权贵贪腐、克扣军饷、荒废军务所致。可此人颠倒黑白、欺瞒君上，不仅不认罪责，反倒借机索要巨额钱粮，实则是想再度借机敛财，充盈派系私库。
未等萧琰出列弹劾，御史大夫已然跨步而出，厉声驳斥。这位御史大夫依附宦官派系，与外戚势力势同水火，句句针锋相对，直言边军溃败绝非钱粮不足，而是外戚派系安插的边将庸碌无能、贪墨渎职、懈怠军务，弹劾户部尚书串通边将、私吞军饷、欺君罔上，请求陛下严查外戚党羽，整顿边军体系。

两人当庭争执，声色俱厉、互揭短处、彼此攻讦。紧随二人之后，外戚派系官员尽数站队，纷纷为户部尚书辩驳，洗白贪腐罪责，将边关战败之责推给军士懈怠、蛮族强悍；宦官派系官员紧随其后，纷纷附议御史大夫的弹劾，大肆控诉外戚专权乱政、祸乱朝纲。一时间，庄严肃穆的金銮大殿，沦为市井骂场，百官吵作一团、喧嚣不止。
无人提及江南洪涝、遍地流民，无人怜悯挨饿受冻的黎民百姓，无人担忧岌岌可危的西北边关，无人正视天下渐起的流民动乱。所有人的争执、辩驳、弹劾、辩解，从来都不是为了社稷安危、天下苍生，只为派系输赢、权力高低、利益得失。赢了，便可打压对手、扩张派系势力；输了，便会折损话语权、失去牟利渠道。朝堂国事，早已沦为派系私斗的工具，万民疾苦，不过是权贵博弈的牺牲品。
萧琰静立班末，冷眼旁观这场荒唐至极的闹剧，心中百感交集，只剩无尽悲凉。他想起数日前，他奉旨前往城南流民安置点巡查灾情的所见所闻。秋雨淅沥，泥泞满地，城南临时安置区破败不堪，低矮的草棚漏雨透风，根本无法遮风避雨。数十万流民拖家带口、衣衫褴褛、面黄肌瘦，老人蜷缩在墙角，瑟瑟发抖、气息奄奄；孩童饿得啼哭不止、面无血色；壮年百姓双目空洞、神情绝望，日日挣扎在生死边缘。
洪涝淹没良田，秋收颗粒无收，百姓失去生计、背井离乡，唯一的期盼便是朝廷的赈灾粮款，能让他们熬过寒冬、得以活命。可朝廷拨付的赈灾银两与粮草，自京城下发，经州府、县衙层层盘剥克扣，抵达流民手中时，早已十不存一。地方官员虚报灾情、冒领赈灾款项，勾结富商囤积粮食、哄抬粮价，趁机大发灾难横财。本该救人的赈灾物资，成了贪官污吏中饱私囊的利器，本该安抚民心的国策，最终变成了压垮百姓的最后一根稻草。
萧琰亲眼看见，有老妇携孙，三日无粮，跪地乞讨，最终饿晕在泥泞之中，再未醒来；亲眼看见，有为生计所迫的壮年百姓，走投无路、含泪卖儿鬻女，只求换一口粗粮活命；亲眼看见，漫天风雨之中，流民尸身无人收敛，草草弃于荒野，任由风雨侵蚀、鸟兽啃食。人间惨剧，莫过于此。
可千里之外的京城，朱门高墙之内，权贵勋贵夜夜笙歌、宴饮不断。琼楼玉宇，灯火璀璨，山珍海味、锦衣玉食，歌舞升平、奢靡无度。他们看不见民间疾苦，听不见流民哀嚎，即便看见听见，也只会漠然置之、无动于衷。于他们而言，底层百姓的生死存亡，从来都无关紧要，只要自己权位稳固、富贵长存，便万事无忧。
归来之后，萧琰彻夜未眠，蘸泪草拟千字灾情疏，将江南洪涝之惨烈、流民之悲苦、地方贪腐之实情尽数列明，字字赤诚、句句泣血，恳请陛下即刻下旨，严查赈灾贪腐官员，足额拨付粮款，安抚流民、减免赋税，修缮堤坝、安抚地方。他以为，纵使帝王倦怠朝政，也该顾念万民、心存恻隐；纵使朝堂浑浊，也该尚存一丝公理良知。
content_en:
In the 27th year of Yong'an in the prosperous Tang Dynasty, in autumn, a frosty wind suddenly rose and swept across Beijing.
The glazed tiles of the Imperial City were covered with a layer of pale white by the overnight cold frost, and the falling morning light did not reflect the grandeur of the centuries-old dynasty. Instead, it made the entire Forbidden City desolate and empty, with the decay of rotten wood everywhere. The duty room at the Yushitai is cold and quiet. Outside the window lattice are the falling dead leaves, and inside the window is the lone figure of Xiao Yan writing and meditating. There is a thick stack of files under his fingertips. The pages are stacked one after another, filled with evidence of the floods in the south of the Yangtze River, the collapse of the northwest frontier army, and the corruption of local officials.
Xiao Yan is twenty-two years old this year and has been an official for twelve years. From a poor family to a new scholar, he has survived to become the censor Zhongcheng. He holds an important position as an official, with the power to supervise hundreds of officials and impeach traitors. In the eyes of outsiders, he has achieved success at a young age and holds an important position. He is a new and important minister with a bright future in the court. But only Xiao Yan himself knew clearly that in the past twelve years of officialdom, what he had seen was never the prosperity of the Qingming Dynasty and the justice of the court, but the layer upon layer of corruption, the greed hidden under the clothes, and the people's hearts and minds that were completely destroyed before the troubled times.
The world is accustomed to praising Dasheng's century-old foundation, saying that the world is at peace, the country is peaceful and the people are safe. But being in the game, Xiao Yan has already seen clearly that this so-called prosperous age is just a false skin whitewashed by the powerful and noble. It has long been rotten inside. The imperial power is weak, foreign relatives are monopolizing power, eunuchs are stealing the government, party disputes are endless, exorbitant taxes have been imposed for many years, and the people are in dire straits. Troubled times never collapse overnight, but fester day after day. People's hearts die first, and then the country collapses. After twelve years of ups and downs, he went through all kinds of situations in the court and saw through the hypocrisy of kings and ministers, the indifference of colleagues, and the greed of powerful people. Finally, he came to a realization: in troubled times, the best way to see people's hearts is, in turbulent times, the best way to distinguish between good and evil.
His half-life of sobriety comes from half a lifetime of blood and tears. Xiao Yan originally belonged to a prominent family in Qingzhou. The Xiao family has been scholarly and loyal for generations. His father, Xiao Jingyuan, was once a royal official of the dynasty. He was upright and upright throughout his life. He took it as his own duty to eliminate corruption and chaos and help the country. He never followed others' influence and was never afraid of the powerful. At that time, Sima Rui, the imperial lieutenant, wielded power between the government and the public, formed cliques for personal gain, controlled government affairs, secretly deducted the salaries of the troops outside the three border fortresses, and enriched his own pockets. As a result, the border troops were cut off from food and grass, their armor was broken, countless border guards died of cold and starvation, and the border defense lines gradually weakened. The civil and military officials in the entire court were afraid of Sima Rui's power, and no one dared to say a word. Only Xiao Jingyuan wrote a memorial all night long, listing his twenty-three major crimes. Every word was sonorous, every sentence was heart-breaking, and he vowed to eliminate traitors for the country and clean up the court.
The bloody fire that night was an indelible mark on Xiao Yan's life. On the execution ground, my father was fearless before his execution, leaving only one last word: The court is chaotic, people's hearts are greedy and delusional, and in troubled times, it is most difficult to keep one's heart. Xiao Yan was still young at that time, full of grief and indignation, only hating traitors and injustice in the world, but he had not yet truly understood that what his father said about greed and chaos in the world was never limited to one or two powerful traitors, but the collective decay of the entire court and the collective failure of countless well-dressed people.
After three years of dormancy, Xiao Yan remained anonymous and studied hard in a cold window, which eliminated the youthful anger and solidified his character and character. He did not choose to hide from the world and live an ignoble existence, but insisted on returning to the capital and setting foot in the court again. When others asked him why he threw himself into a trap and returned to troubled times, he only replied: If all the loyal ministers shun the world and all the good ministers keep silent, this great country will be completely hopeless. He wants to become an official, establish a dynasty, see the chaos of the turbulent dynasty with his own eyes, and use his own meager efforts to keep the court clear and bright, and comfort the loyal souls of the whole family.
At the end of his weak crown, Xiao Yan returned to the golden list and entered the court as an official with the first place in the second class of the imperial examination. He abandoned all old family grudges, did not cling to powerful people, did not join factions, and stood alone in the turbulent court. When he first entered the official career, he still retained the sincerity of youth, firmly believed that justice was in the heart of the people, firmly believed that loyalty and kindness would have repercussions, and firmly believed that as long as an official was honest and performed his duties, he would be able to bring order to the people and bring peace to the people. But in twelve years, I have seen it with my own eyes countless times,His personal and heart-breaking experience crushed all his innocent expectations bit by bit, allowing him to fully understand the nature of the court in troubled times.
Today's Dasheng has long been prosperous on the outside but dry on the inside, with gold and jade in ruins. Emperor Yong'an reigned for twenty-seven years. In his early years, he still had the ambition to work hard for governance. However, in his later years, he became tired of government affairs, indulged in immortality elixirs, indulged in pleasures in the palace, and ignored state affairs and the people all day long. The imperial power gradually fell into disuse, and the huge court became a chess game played by three forces: relatives, eunuchs, and aristocratic families. The three parties check and balance each other, compete with each other, and the other ebbs and flows. No one cares about the safety of the country, and no one cares about the suffering of the people. What everyone wants in life is only power, fame, and wealth.
The foreign relatives, headed by Taiwei Sima Rui, relied on the power of the concubines in the harem to control the military and political affairs of the court, and controlled the military power of the capital. Their descendants and relatives were spread all over the government and the public, occupying half of the positions of the three officials and nine ministers. They wantonly amassed money, planted private parties, and suppressed dissidents. They were so arrogant that no one dared to check and balance them. The eunuchs, headed by Wei Bingqian, the eunuch in charge of the ceremonial department, held the power of approving the emperor, managed affairs on behalf of the emperor, controlled the access of documents and edicts in the court, secretly made friends with officials from poor families and local vassals, formed cliques for personal gain, deceived the saints, tampered with government orders, misinterpreted the holy will, and profited from it. The old aristocratic families have been entrenched in the government and the public for hundreds of years, clinging to their family status, marrying each other, and monopolizing the name of the court. They seem to be noble and self-sufficient, but in fact they protect themselves and sit back and watch the success or failure. They will rely on whoever is in power, and they have no trace of the character of the family and the country.
In addition to the three core factions, the remaining officials are even more disorganized and have their own agendas. Some people follow the power and try to get everything they want, just to live a stable life and get promoted step by step; some people are greedy, plunder people's fat, and regard official positions as profit-making merchants; some people are mediocre and do nothing, but achieve nothing in high positions; some people are timid and silent, seeing traitors running rampant and people's livelihood suffering, but they always protect themselves and dare not say anything. In the huge Dasheng court, there are hundreds of civil and military officials, but there are only a few who truly care about their country, their people, and stick to their true intentions.
Xiao Yan stood in this turbid chess game, like a lonely boat floating in the sea, surrounded by turbidity, but he was the only one who was clear. In the past twelve years, he has seen too many hypocritical faces, seen through too many cold hearts, and gradually understood that the chaos in the world begins with chaos in the heart. The collapse of mountains and rivers begins with the collapse of people's hearts, and the overthrow of societies begins with the loss of people's hearts. In the peaceful and prosperous times, there were still restraints by etiquette and law, and moral restraints, and people still knew their integrity, understood loyalty, and kept the bottom line. However, in troubled times, the laws are loose, the imperial power is weak, and there is no one to check and balance. The greed, selfishness, cruelty, and cunning in the depths of human nature are all exposed. All loyalty, etiquette, and the righteousness of the family and country have become empty talk that can be discarded and trampled on at will.
Today at Mao hour, the sky has not yet dawned, and the morning fog is thick, covering the entire imperial city. Outside the Meridian Gate, there were cars and horses passing by, and crowns and crowns like clouds. The moment of entering the court, which should have been a solemn and solemn moment, was instead filled with market-like businessmanship and flattery. The officials were in small groups, chatting in low voices. No one discussed the pros and cons of border defense and military affairs and people's livelihood. Every sentence was filled with factional trends, emperors' wishes, and promotion opportunities. Some people whispered to inquire about the concubine's recent preferences, hoping to please her and cling to her relatives; some people secretly inquired about the movements of the Supervisor of Ceremonies, hoping to rely on the eunuch and seek convenience; some people flattered and exchanged greetings with each other, pretending to be friends, but in fact they had their own plans and were wary of each other.
Xiao Yan was dressed in a plain green robe and stood at the end of the crowd. He had a tall and straight posture, and his eyebrows were clear and cool without any hint of violence. He has long been accustomed to such noisy and hypocritical scenes, and has already seen through the true face of these well-dressed people. In front of others, everyone is a humble gentleman and a loyal and virtuous minister, while behind everyone, everyone is a coward and selfish person. Twelve years of experience in officialdom had smoothed his youthful spirit, but not his true character. He had only learned to observe with a cold eye, observe silently, not to get involved in factional disputes, not to participate in the game of fame and fortune, and only to abide by his duties as censor, to observe the mistakes of all officials, and to sympathize with the suffering of all people.
Today’s court meeting is the most solemn meeting in the monthThe meeting was supposed to decide on several major issues related to the survival of the country. First, the autumn rains in the seven counties in the south of the Yangtze River continued for three months. Rivers overflowed, dams collapsed, and thousands of hectares of fertile farmland were flooded. Hundreds of thousands of people were displaced and suffered from hunger and cold. The disaster was tragic. The government urgently needed to provide disaster relief, repair dams, and reduce taxes. Secondly, the barbarians in the northwest took advantage of the autumn season and repeatedly invaded the border. They broke through three border fortresses, plundered border villages and towns, and massacred the people in the border areas. However, the Dasheng border army was depleted in armaments, lacked food and grass, and was disorganized. The defenders were afraid of the enemy and avoided fighting, and were retreating steadily. The northwest border defense was in danger. Thirdly, taxes in prefectures and counties all over the world are heavy and heavy. Local officials have increased taxes and imposed corvee arbitrarily. The people are overwhelmed. Refugees have gathered in many places to cause trouble, and there are faint signs of unrest.
Each and every one of them is a hidden danger of national subjugation and chaos, and they are all important matters related to the life and death of thousands of people and the survival of Dasheng. But Xiao Yan knew in his heart that such a crisis, in the eyes of the powerful people in the court, was just a chess piece for gaming and an opportunity to make profits, and no one ever really took it to heart.
In the Jinluan Hall, smoke curled up, solemnly and solemnly. On the high position, Emperor Yong'an sat quietly with his eyes lowered. His face was tired, his eyes were cloudy, and he no longer had any imperial aura. Sitting on the dragon's throne, he seems to be in control of the world, but in fact, his mind has been consumed by the pleasures in the palace. He turns a blind eye and hears nothing about the chaos in the court and the suffering in the world. All he wanted was the stability of the imperial power, longevity, and happiness for the rest of his life. As for the displacement of the people, dangers at the border, and hidden dangers to the country, they were not worth mentioning.
At the beginning of the court meeting, the Minister of Hubu took the lead in going out to start the memorial. This person belongs to the foreign relatives' faction and is a confidant single-handedly promoted by Sima Rui. He holds an important position in the Ministry of Household Affairs and is in charge of the world's money, food and taxes. However, he never cares about managing the people's finances. He only takes it as his own duty to line his own pockets and subsidize his relatives and clan. He held a memorial in his hand and spoke sincerely. He cried out every sentence about the difficulties of the northwest frontier army. He lied about the shortage of food and grass at the border, old ordnance and insufficient troops. He implored your majesty to allocate five million taels of silver and 100,000 stones of food and grass to reorganize the frontier army and resist foreign enemies.
As soon as these words came out, Xiao Yan felt a chill in his heart. He had just received a secret report from the border three days ago. Most of the 3 million taels of military pay and 200,000 shi of food and grass allocated by the imperial court in the first half of the year were secretly withheld by the border army guards and officials from the Ministry of Household Affairs. They were transferred layer by layer and eventually fell into the private treasury of Sima Rui's relatives' group. Less than 30% actually reached the military camp and was used for sergeants. The current defeat of the border army is not due to insufficient allocation by the court, but due to the corruption of the powerful, the deduction of military pay, and the neglect of military affairs. But this person confuses right and wrong and deceives the emperor. Not only does he not admit his guilt, but he takes the opportunity to ask for huge amounts of money and food. In fact, he wants to take the opportunity to make money again and fill the faction's private treasury.
Before Xiao Yan came out to impeach him, the imperial censor had already stepped out and refuted it sharply. This imperial censor attached himself to the eunuch faction and was in the same position as his foreign relatives. He spoke tit-for-tat. He bluntly stated that the defeat of the border army was not due to lack of money and food, but because the border generals installed by the foreign relatives' faction were mediocre and incompetent, corrupt and derelict in their duties, and neglected military affairs. He impeached the Minister of Hubu for colluding with the border generals, embezzling military pay, and bullying the emperor. He requested Your Majesty to strictly investigate the foreign relatives' gang members and rectify the frontier army system.
The two argued in court, with both strong voices and strong voices, exposing each other's shortcomings and criticizing each other. Following the two men, all the officials from the foreign relatives faction stood in line, defending the Minister of the Ministry of Revenue, clearing away the blame for corruption, and blaming the failure of the border war on the slackness of the sergeants and the toughness of the barbarians. The officials from the eunuch faction followed closely behind, and they all supported the impeachment of the imperial censor, and they accused the foreign relatives of monopolizing power and disrupting the government and disrupting the imperial court. For a time, the solemn Jinluan Hall was reduced to a scolding scene in the market, with officials quarreling and noisy.
No one mentioned the floods in the south of the Yangtze River and the refugees everywhere, no one pitied the hungry and cold civilians, no one worried about the precarious northwest border, and no one faced the rising refugee unrest in the world. Everyone's disputes, arguments, impeachments, and excuses are never for the safety of the country or the common people, but only for the victory or defeat of factions, the level of power, and the gain and loss of interests. If you win, you can suppress your opponent.Expand the faction's power; if you lose, you will lose your right to speak and lose your profit-making channels. State affairs in the court have long been reduced to a tool for private fighting between factions, and the suffering of the people is nothing but a victim of the game between the powerful.
Xiao Yan stood quietly at the end of the class, watching this ridiculous farce with a cold eye, feeling mixed feelings in her heart, leaving only endless sadness. He recalled what he saw and heard a few days ago when he was ordered to go to the refugee resettlement site in the south of the city to inspect the disaster situation. The autumn rain was pouring, and the ground was covered with mud. The temporary resettlement area in the south of the city was in a dilapidated state. The low thatched sheds were leaky and ventilated, providing no shelter from the wind and rain. Hundreds of thousands of refugees are dragging their families with them, wearing ragged clothes and looking sallow and thin. The elderly are huddled in the corner, shivering and dying; the children are crying from hunger and their faces are pale; the people in their prime have empty eyes and expressions of despair, struggling on the edge of life and death every day.
Floods submerged fertile fields, and the autumn harvest failed. People lost their livelihoods and left their homes. Their only hope was the government's disaster relief food funds, which could enable them to survive the cold winter. However, the disaster relief silver and grain and grass allocated by the imperial court were distributed from the capital, and were exploited and exploited by state and county governments at all levels. By the time they reached the hands of the refugees, not even a tenth of them was left. Local officials falsely reported the disaster situation, pretended to receive relief funds, colluded with wealthy businessmen to hoard food, and drove up food prices, taking advantage of the disaster to make a fortune. Disaster relief materials that were supposed to save people became a weapon for corrupt officials to line their own pockets. National policies that were supposed to appease the people eventually became the last straw that broke the people's hearts.
Xiao Yan saw with his own eyes an old woman and her grandson who had been without food for three days and knelt down to beg, and finally fainted from hunger in the mud and never woke up again. There is no greater tragedy in the world than this.
But thousands of miles away in the capital, within the high walls of the royal gates, the dignitaries and nobles were singing and feasting every night. The palace is decorated with bright lights, delicacies from the mountains and seas, fine clothes and food, singing and dancing, and extravagance. They cannot see the suffering of the people and cannot hear the cries of the refugees. Even if they see and hear it, they will just ignore it and be indifferent. For them, the life and death of the people at the bottom has never mattered. As long as their power and status are stable and their wealth lasts, they will have nothing to worry about.
After returning, Xiao Yan stayed up all night and drafted a thousand words about the disaster with tears in his eyes. He listed the brutality of the floods in the south of the Yangtze River, the misery of the refugees, and the true situation of local corruption. Every word was sincere and every sentence was bloody, and he implored His Majesty to immediately issue an order to strictly investigate the corrupt officials involved in disaster relief, allocate sufficient food funds, appease the refugees, reduce taxes, repair dams, and appease the local area. He believes that even if the emperor is tired of government affairs, he should still care about all the people and have compassion; even if the court is muddy, there should still be a trace of justice and conscience.
